messages.content: is the tree grow last year correct?
use the tree grew last year. grew is the word for that past sentence.
now say it happens every year.
the tree grows every year.
can i say the tree is growing?
yes. it can say the tree is getting larger now or over the time you are talking about.
make that explanation shorter.
yes. the tree is growing can be about a change happening now.
what if i only saw one picture from last year?
then you cannot know all its changes now from that picture alone. you would need more information about the tree today.
only give the sentence about last year.
the tree grew last year.
can you know how much?
no. the sentence gives a change, but not how large the change was.
write a longer story about a child moving a page before helping clean a table. show why the order is useful without making it a rule for every task.

a child came into the kitchen and saw water on the table near a page his sister had written. his mother asked for help cleaning. before he went to get a towel, he moved the page to a place on the shelf where the water could not reach it. then he brought the towel and helped with the table. his sister came in while they were finishing and asked where her page was. he showed her and explained the order he had chosen. getting the towel was useful, but moving the page first had kept it away from the water while he was gone. after the table was ready, she put the page back and read what she had written. he had thought about what could happen while he did each part of the task.
what did he do first?
he moved the page away from the water.
why not leave it there while getting a towel?
it was near water. moving it away first kept the page out of the water while he got a towel.
make that explanation shorter.
he moved the page before leaving so the water would not reach it.
can you know this order is always best for every cleaning task?
no. it worked for the details in this story. another task might need a different order.
finish with his sister finding her place again.
she sat at the clean table, found the last line on the page, and began writing again.
i have two ideas for a story. i do not want to choose one yet.
you can keep both for now. what is different about them?
one is about a child at school, and one is about a family going to another town.
those give you different places and groups of people to work with.
should i make both into one story just because i have them now?
not unless that is what you want. you can keep each idea on its own page and choose later whether they go together.
make that explanation shorter.
you can keep two ideas without putting them together yet.
help me write a short note for each, using only what i told you.
a story about a child at school. a story about a family going to another town.
why not add that the child is sad?
you did not give that feeling. the idea can stay open until you choose the people and what happens.
now give a made up next part for the school one.
the child finds a page in a book and asks the teacher who wrote it.
can you know that should be in my real plan?
no. it is a possible made up part, not a choice you have already made.
can watch be an object and something i do?
yes. a watch is a thing used to know the time. watch can also be about looking at something over time.
make that explanation shorter.
a watch is a thing for time. watch can also be something you do.
if i say i left my watch on the table, is that about looking?
no. my watch is the object in that sentence.
now make a sentence about looking at a film.
i watch a film with my sister.
can you ask what i watched yesterday?
what did you watch yesterday?
why watch after did?
did goes with watch in the question. watched works without did when saying i watched a film yesterday.
only give the object sentence again.
i left my watch on the table.
i want to hear the story my brother is telling, but i only have five minutes before work. help me say that clearly.
i would like to hear your story, but i only have five minutes before work. is that enough time, or should we choose another time?
can i keep it shorter?
i want to hear it, but i only have five minutes now. would another time be better?
what if he says it is very short?
then you can choose to listen now if you want. you have told him how much time you have, so he can use that information too.
make that explanation shorter.
you have told him your time, and he can say whether it is enough.
what could he tell me about the story?
he can tell you whether five minutes is enough for his story.
only give the question about another time again.
would another time be better?
why not say i do not care about the story?
because that is not what you said. having little time now is different from choosing not to hear it.
write a longer story about a child choosing a small book and learning that the size outside does not give the whole reading time.

a child chose a small book from the shelf because he had only a little time before dinner. it was easy to carry, and he thought it would take little time to finish. when he opened it, he saw many pages with small writing. another book on the table was larger, but each page had only a few words next to a picture. he asked his father which one would take less time to read. his father said they should look inside, not choose from the outside size alone. the child chose one short story from the small book rather than trying to finish the whole thing. the small size still made it easy to carry, but it had not told him everything about the task.
what had he known from holding the book?
it was small and easy to carry.
what had he not checked yet?
how much writing was inside and how long the reading might take.
explain what he learned from opening the books.
he learned to look at the pages before choosing what he could read in the time he had.
why was one story a useful choice?
it was a smaller reading goal than finishing the whole book before dinner.
finish with the book ready for later too.
he put a small note at the next story and left the book on the shelf. he could return when he had more time.
i have seven objects. four are red and three are blue. can you know which are the objects my sister has as her own?
no. you have not said which objects your sister has as her own.
make that explanation shorter.
color alone does not tell whose they are.
now i say all three blue objects are hers, and the four red objects are mine.
then your sister has three objects, and you have four.
say which color each person has.
the three blue objects are hers, and the four red objects are yours.
if she gives me one blue object, how many do i have?
five objects: four red and one blue.
does the blue object become red because it is mine now?
no. changing whose it is does not change its color.
only give how many blue objects i have now.
one.
does almost always mean always?
no. almost always says it happens very often, but leaves open that it may not happen on some days.
make that explanation shorter.
almost always leaves room for a day when it does not happen.
can i say i almost always read before bed if one day i did not?
yes. that sentence can leave room for that day.
can i say i never read then?
no. never would be the opposite idea from reading very often.
what if i want to talk only about yesterday?
then say what happened yesterday: i did not read before bed yesterday.
does that change what i do most days?
not by itself. one day does not tell us what you do on all the other days.
make that answer shorter.
one day is not the whole story of what you usually do.
only give the yesterday sentence again.
i did not read before bed yesterday.
make a short message from these facts: i am home, the book is on the table, and i will call after dinner. do not add why.
i am home. the book is on the table, and i will call after dinner.
can you make it one sentence?
i am home, the book is on the table, and i will call after dinner.
does that tell us whose book it is?
no. you said the book, but did not give whose it is.
now it is the book of my sister, and the message is to her. use your.
i am home, your book is on the table, and i will call after dinner.
why your instead of her?
because you are talking to your sister in that message. your speaks to the person reading it.
use words without speaks.
your is for the person you are talking to in the message.
only give the message again.
i am home, your book is on the table, and i will call after dinner.
write a longer story about someone telling a story from the middle and another person asking what happened before. use simple words.

a child came into the room saying that the book was back on the shelf now. his father did not know which book had been moved or why. the child began with the last part because the first parts were still clear in his own mind. his father asked him to start with where the book had been that morning. then the child explained that his sister had taken it to read, left it on the table, and finally put it back. the father could follow the small story once he knew what had changed. the last sentence had been true all along, but it was more clear with the first parts given too. after that, the child asked which part his father wanted to hear more about.
why did the father need more information?
he had not heard the first parts and did not know what back was about.
why had the child started at the end?
the child knew the parts before, but his father had not heard them.
make that answer shorter.
he knew more of the story than his father did.
what useful question did the father ask?
where was the book this morning?
finish with the short story in the right order.
his sister had taken the book from the shelf, read it at the table, and put it back. now his father knew the whole order.
my friend and i used the same word for different things. i want to say i understand their meaning now without saying my whole idea was wrong.
i understand how you are using that word now. i was using it for something different.
make that message shorter.
i understand your meaning now. i had a different one in mind.
can i ask them to give an example next time?
yes. you could add: an example would help me know which meaning you want.
put the message together.
i understand how you are using that word now. i was using it for something different. an example would help me know which meaning you want.
can you make it shorter?
i understand your meaning now. an example would help next time.
why not say words can mean anything?
because words still need context. a word can have more than one meaning, but the sentence should help make the right one clear.
make that explanation shorter.
context helps people know which meaning you want.
that message is enough. do not add more.
okay. i will leave it there.
just give a kind goodbye.
goodbye, and take care.
now one word.
goodbye.
